source: Karnataka NMMS MAT 2023-24 question paper, NMMS-MAT (K-8) P-1 (pyq/ka-2023-24-mat.pdf). The paper has no answer key, so every answer here is worked out by us.

questions.prompt:
A + B means 'A' is the father of 'B'; A × B means 'A' is the brother of 'B'; A = B means 'A' is the daughter of 'B'.
If P × R = Q, which statement is correct?
questions.rule: Read each sign in turn: P × R means P is the brother of R, and R = Q means R is the daughter of Q.
questions.working: P is the brother of Q’s daughter, so P is a son of Q.

questions.prompt:
A + B means 'A' is the father of 'B'; A × B means 'A' is the brother of 'B'; A = B means 'A' is the daughter of 'B'.
If X + Y = Z, which statement is wrong?
questions.rule: X + Y means X is the father of Y, and Y = Z means Y is the daughter of Z.
questions.working: X is the father, a man, so he cannot be the sister of Y. (Z is Y’s other parent, the mother, so the wife of X.)

questions.prompt: A and B are brothers, C and D are sisters. The son of A is the brother of D. What is B to C?
questions.rule: Find how the two families join: A's son is the brother of D, so A is the father of D, and so of D's sister C.
questions.working: B is A's brother, so B is C's uncle.

questions.prompt: Which of the cubes (1)–(4) can be formed when this net is folded into a cube?
questions.rule: In a straight line of squares, the 1st and 3rd are opposite; two squares stuck on opposite sides of the line are opposite too.

questions.prompt: Two positions of a dice are shown. How many dots are on the face opposite the face with 3 dots?
questions.rule: A face can never be opposite a face seen next to it.
questions.working: In the first view 2 is beside 4 and 1, in the second beside 3 and 6, so 5 is opposite 2. Turning the first view about the 2 face brings 3 to the bottom, under 4: 4 is opposite 3.

questions.prompt: The six faces of a cube are marked ○, ●, +, *, − and □. Three positions of the cube are shown. Which net does the cube unfold into?
questions.rule: First find the opposite pairs: a face cannot be opposite a face seen next to it.
questions.working: □ is seen next to ●, ○, + and −, so □ is opposite *. + and − are seen together, so ○ and ● are each opposite one of them; turning the views to match shows ○ is opposite + and ● is opposite −. Only net D keeps all three pairs apart.

questions.prompt: Which of these years is not a leap year?
questions.rule: A century year (ending in 00) is a leap year only if it divides by 400.
questions.working: 700 does not divide by 400, so it is not a leap year.
questions.note: 650 is not a leap year either (it does not divide by 4), so A and B both fit. The paper probably meant century years only; check the official key.

questions.prompt: If Independence Day in 2021 was on a Sunday, on which day of the week will Independence Day be in 2025?

questions.working: From 15 August 2021 to 15 August 2025: 2022 +1, 2023 +1, 2024 +2 (29 February 2024), 2025 +1 = 5 days. Sunday + 5 = Friday

questions.prompt: What is the total number of days in the years 2023 and 2024?

questions.working: 2023 has 365 days and 2024 (a leap year) has 366: 365 + 366 = 731

questions.prompt: Ravi walks 8 km north from his house. Then he turns right and walks 4 km, then turns right and walks 8 km. Again he turns left and walks 10 km. How far is Ravi from his house now?

questions.working: North 8, right (east) 4, right (south) 8, left (east) 10. He is back level with the house, 4 + 10 = 14 km east of it.

questions.prompt: One morning Raju and Satish were talking face to face by the road. If Satish's shadow is exactly to the right of Raju, which direction is Satish facing?
questions.rule: In the morning the sun is in the east, so shadows fall to the west.
questions.working: Satish's shadow falls west, and it is to Raju's right. Raju faces Satish; if west is on Raju's right, Raju faces south, so Satish faces north.

questions.prompt: A man is facing north-east. He turns 90° clockwise and then 135° anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?

questions.working: North-east + 90° clockwise = south-east; then 135° anticlockwise = north. (45° + 90° − 135° = 0°)

questions.prompt:
A, B, C, D and E sit around a circular table facing the centre. 'E' sits second to the right of 'D'. 'C' sits second to the right of 'E'. 'A' does not sit next to 'D'.
Who sits to the right of 'A'?
questions.rule: Place D, then E two seats to D's right and C two seats to E's right. The two seats left are next to D on one side and between E and C; A cannot be next to D, so A sits between E and C and B next to D.
questions.working: Going to the right from D: D, B, E, A, C. So C is to A's right.

questions.prompt:

questions.rule: Place D, then E two seats to D's right and C two seats to E's right. The two seats left are next to D on one side and between E and C; A cannot be next to D, so A sits between E and C and B next to D.
questions.working: Going to the right from D: D, B, E, A, C. So B sits between D and E.
